capabilities: Movement, physical props, constraints, fracture, traveling projectiles, lightning, particles and bounded fluids share gameplay and presentation. The closeout report records core, visible editor and mixed exported-world checks.
Bounded acceptance only. Unsupported fracture uses generic debris; conservative collision, heightfield liquids and fixed fog domains remain. Cloth, soft bodies and ragdolls are absent.
Shared player controller provides sprint resources, double jump, directional dodge, lunge, crouch, prone, slide and grapple traversal with collision.
Source presence is not complete visible or clean-machine validation. Consult the current requirement sign-off for acceptance and remaining gates.
Runtime attacks, healing, health, target selection, pursuit and caster-attached cone presentation share the adventure runtime.
Damage and health values are provisional. Finished character assets and complete milestone sign-off remain deferred or open; see current evidence.
Crowd control and boss break bars
Fourteen control effects, player anti-chain immunity and boss break/stagger/recovery states have explicit runtime representations.
Boss behavior is distinct from PvP immunity. Per-effect source and tests must be inspected; this catalogue does not certify balance or full gameplay completion.
Optional searchable lessons share one visible entry point across editing modes.
Text guidance with saved reading positions; live appearance and input verification pending. Not interactive task tracking.
Exploration and the existing editing tools operate on the same authored scene; gameplay tests use a separate temporary copy.
Experimental preview. Physical input, complete visual acceptance, objectives, XP and unlocks are not established.
Saved bounded events, conditions and actions share one runtime across editor Play and Windows export; authoring supports Undo and independent Play state.

Collection, interaction and spherical area events with item/objective conditions and objective/door/finish actions. Shared character movement and combat now exist; final Step 4/4A acceptance remains open. No arbitrary scripting. Check current validation evidence separately.
Packages the standalone player, engine and C++ runtime libraries with an integrity-checked portable scene.
Package validation does not prove visible play, clean-machine compatibility, code signing, or non-Windows support.

The active build assembles a native Win32 editor, core library, session library, renderer and physics DLLs, native project host, project modules and checks. Python orchestrates compilation; it is not the editor runtime.
Windows/D3D12 is the current build contract. Compiling successfully does not validate runtime behavior or portable packaging.

The native editor keeps floating controls over the canvas, beginner/advanced settings, terrain and shape tools, named colors and a full feature catalogue. The catalogue describes both experimental tools and unimplemented ambitions.
A catalogue entry is not proof of a working subsystem. Latest saved UI evidence is described separately.
Current Play uses the main editor renderer/session in both window modes. Retained GamePreview code can own a secondary session but is not the current Play command path.
Independent views consume additional resources; this is not a demonstrated shared GPU resource pool or a packaged game exporter.
SceneData models authored objects, terrain, liquid sources, environment and ray-tracing preferences. Character records also represent props. JSON serialization and validation are native C++.
This is a record/vector model, not evidence of a general archetype ECS. Saved authored state differs from a simulation checkpoint.
The writer emits NativeScene V7 and the viewport accepts versions V1–V7. The binary packet is distinct from JSON scene schema and project/preset schemas.
Native exports remain active ABI boundaries even though the managed editor was retired.
The native command layer provides describe/inspect and transactional add, move, route, rename, remove, configure, shape, transform and terrain operations with expected scene hashes.
This is local command automation. It is not an embedded AI model, cloud service, or complete GUI command parity.
Platform and command code implement native file handling, hashed scene revisions and save protection; editor history supports undo/redo and canceled edits.
Whole-scene history and asset portability need separate memory and distribution policies. No unlimited-history safety claim is made.
Editable terrain has 97×97 height samples at 0.25 m spacing over a 24 m span. It supports brushes, surface painting and denser preview geometry.
A heightfield cannot encode caves or stacked surfaces. Rendering currently rebuilds geometry; this is not world streaming.
Native mesh code provides transforms, bounds/picking and sculpt operations on authored mesh copies, with scene history integration.
Do not infer topology repair, adaptive remeshing, UV authoring or a production sculpting package.
The scene shape list includes basic solids, rocks, pebbles, grass, fire/light/lava, Chaos Lightning, Chaos Rock, Light-Bound Shard and Craxis Smoke.
Procedural props are not a world scatter, foliage simulation, fracture or particle system.
The native asset path parses GLB geometry and validates accessors, buffers and graph structure for preview meshes.
Creator static import must not be credited with skinning/animation capability. Full imported material/animation authoring is not established.

Search asset folders by name and type; insert models, native objects, groups and scene objects. Save native templates/groups, copy selections between scenes, repair missing models, and export portable scene or selection folders with integrity manifests.

Text browser has no thumbnails. Native templates exclude imported models; portable scene folders support embedded GLB dependencies. This is editor-content reuse, not standalone game export. GUI visual acceptance and clean-machine validation remain separate.
NativeSession owns a worker thread with coalesced scene/camera/control input. It exposes status, capture, playback and suspend/resume. Viewport and physics work are owned by the session path.
Resize now preserves the viewport/device and replaces size-dependent images; scene changes can still rebuild geometry. Worker ownership is not a proof of race freedom.
The viewport explicitly selects native output and disables the upscaler request. HDR rendering, spatial edge AA and presentation use the shared D3D12 renderer.
No super resolution or frame generation is allowed for current acceptance. Native resolution does not guarantee alias-free output.
DxrPass builds acceleration structures and executes compute inline RayQuery, with selectable tiers and raster fallback. The shader build targets cs_6_5.

This is not an RT state-object/shader-table pipeline. Historical device-loss failures remain dated evidence; current throughput requires a successful run with explicit workload, native dimensions and presentation conditions.
The native wavelet path implements prefilter, temporal reconstruction, atrous filtering and composition, with history/guide resources.
ABI mode 0 is native wavelet. Existence of the implementation is not fresh runtime validation or proof of zero ghosting.
Direct NGX integration supplies optional Ray Reconstruction and capability/failure handling. The denoiser API maps mode 1 to RR and mode 0 to wavelet.
RR must remain 1:1. Vendor capability, local SDK/DLL paths and fallback behavior require explicit validation; no super-resolution authorization follows from RR.
Atmosphere compute shaders provide injection, integration and composition; scene settings include time of day, day cycle and fog. Local lights and smoke are packet inputs.
Bounded froxel fog and procedural skies are not a full weather or fluid-smoke solver. Raster and ray visibility differ.
The native physics DLL integrates Jolt with fixed stepping, collision shape preparation and a job system. The editor wrapper consumes body poses and liquid data.
Async collision cooks and four-worker Jolt scheduling are not a global concurrency budget. High-density coupled performance remains unverified.
TerrainFlow maintains separate water/lava arrays on a 48×48 grid, with 0.5 m cells, obstacle coverage and geometry extraction.
This is terrain-bound surface transport, not a general 3D incompressible fluid solver or guaranteed two-way pressure coupling.
Objects carry X/Z route points and speed; NativeSession implements repeat/follow and playback/reset behavior.
Route playback is distinct from navigation, skeletal locomotion, collision-aware character controllers and animation graphs.
Native music controls use Windows MCI with playlist/playback/volume behavior.
Editor music is not a spatial audio engine or exported game soundtrack system.
The shared texture loader supports DDS block-compressed textures, mip selection and format-aware GPU uploads, alongside existing image loading.
A BC5/BC7 loader is not a complete editor PBR material library, offline cooker or asynchronous residency manager.
The native host loads project modules through StarlightRunProject; editor project handling validates schema 3 manifests and launches/reconciles presets.
Creator scene Play and project-DLL execution are separate workflows. See current publication and closeout evidence for tested export cases; project-host and editor-player workflows remain distinct.
PersistentWorkers uses contiguous ranges, caller participation, condition variables and a shared completion count. Threads are joined on destruction.
This class does not implement a general task DAG, fibers or work stealing. Wider thread counts require measured gains, not utilization alone.
The renderer owns command lists/allocators, barriers, submission and frame retirement. CPU parallel preparation does not automatically imply concurrent D3D12 recording.
Future parallel recording needs per-worker/per-slot ownership, reserved bindings and ordered resource transitions.
Native checks cover core data, controlled diagnostics, textures, UI, sessions and render harnesses. The audit GUI coordinates checks and preserves result files.
Checks are evidence for their exact run, not blanket certification. This analyzer does not run them or change failed assertions.
The current source contains auditOffscreen and optional benchmark exports. These are committed diagnostic facilities, not an accepted gameplay rendering mode.

Historical renderer failures are preserved; newer Gate 0 evidence and the reliability checkpoint record an isolated output-target correction. A source scan alone does not certify matched performance or lifecycle reliability.
